extracted.intended_audience: students of mathematical logic (undergraduate/graduate) or readers learning formal syntax and semantics
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, theorems, and notational conventions for syntax (terms, atomic formulas, wffs, free variables, sentences), computability/enumerability notions, and the semantic notion of structures and satisfaction in first-order logic. Includes constructive procedures (enumeration/dovetailing) and examples of translation between English and formal language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semidecidable (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set A of expressions is semidecidable iff there exists an effective procedure that, given any expression ε, produces the answer “yes” iff ε ∈ A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ε ∉ A the procedure may never give an answer; this asymmetry is what distinguishes semidecidability from decidability. The text illustrates using a listing: watch the enumeration and say “yes” if ε appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectively enumerable ⇔ semidecidable (Theorem 17E)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set is effectively enumerable iff it is semidecidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea (constructive): given semidecision procedure, enumerate all expressions ε1, ε2, ... and apply dovetailing (time-sharing) scheme: test ε1 for one minute, then ε1 and ε2 for two minutes, then ε1,ε2,ε3 for three minutes, etc.; whenever procedure outputs “yes,” output that expression (avoid duplicates). Conversely, if set is effectively enumerable, semidecision is done by watching the enumeration for ε. Notes the practical impossibility of knowing non-membership from finite absence in listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decidable set (characterization, Theorem 17F)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of expressions is decidable iff both it and its complement (relative to all expressions) are effectively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is sometimes called Kleene's theorem. Intuitively, two semidecision procedures (one for A and one for complement) combine to yield a decision procedure. (Proof assigned as exercise.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure properties of effectively enumerable and decidable sets
rubrics_metrics.description: If sets A and B are effectively enumerable, then so are A ∪ B and A ∩ B. The class of decidable sets is closed under union, intersection, and complementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closure under union/intersection for enumerable sets is asserted (Exercise 11). For decidable sets, closure under complement is immediate and union/intersection follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerability of tautological consequences (Theorem 17G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Σ is a decidable (or effectively enumerable) set of wffs, then the set of tautological consequences of Σ is effectively enumerable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: enumerate sentences σ1,σ2,... from Σ; given any wff τ, test successively whether ∅ |= τ, {σ1} |= τ, {σ1,σ2} |= τ, ... using truth tables; by the (corollary to) compactness theorem, if Σ |= τ then some finite subset entails τ, so this procedure will eventually answer “yes.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective computability of functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A function f is effectively computable (computable) iff there exists an effective procedure that, given an input x, will eventually produce the correct output f(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The textbook states the definition succinctly; this is the model of algorithmic computability used here (informal/effective procedure).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-order language specification (what to fix)
rubrics_metrics.description: To specify a first-order language one must (i) say whether the equality symbol is present and (ii) specify the parameters: predicate symbols (by arity), constant symbols, and function symbols (by arity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text lists the logical symbols (parentheses, →, ¬, variables, equality optional) and parameter categories, and gives concrete example languages (pure predicate language, language of set theory, language of elementary number theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of equality symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: The equality symbol '=' is optional; if present it is treated as a logical symbol rather than a parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Its status as a logical symbol (not a parameter) affects its behavior under translations into English and in model-theoretic interpretation: = is interpreted as actual equality in structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms are expressions built up from variables and constant symbols by prefixing function symbols: for each n-place function symbol f, apply F_f(ε1,...,εn) = f ε1 ... εn. Terms are exactly those expressions obtainable by zero or more such operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polish notation is used for function symbols (function at left), terms do not contain parentheses or commas. Examples: + v2 S0, SSSS0, + E v1 SS0 E v2 SS0. Unique readability of terms (unique decomposition) will be proved later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic formulas (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An atomic formula is an expression of the form P t1 ... tn where P is an n-place predicate symbol and t1,...,tn are terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atomic formulas play the role analogous to sentence symbols in sentential logic; examples: = v1 v2, ∈ v5 v3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-formed formulas (wffs) (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wffs are expressions built up from atomic formulas by applying (zero or more times) the formula-building operations E_¬(γ) = (¬ γ), E_→(γ,δ) = (γ → δ), and Q_i(γ) = ∀ v_i γ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the inductive/recursive construction of all formulas; unique readability of wffs (unique decomposition) is asserted to hold and will be proved later (Section 2.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Free variable (recursive definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any variable x and wff α, x occurs free in α iff (1) for atomic α, x occurs free iff x occurs in α; (2) x free in (¬ α) iff x free in α; (3) x free in (α → β) iff x free in α or β; (4) x free in ∀ v_i α iff x free in α and x ≠ v_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recursive definition is cast in terms of a function h mapping wffs to sets of free variables; existence/uniqueness of h follows from the recursion theorem. If no variable occurs free (h(α)=∅), α is a sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sentence is a wff in which no variable occurs free (i.e., h(α)=∅).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentences are the wffs translatable into English without blanks and are typically the most interesting wffs; non-sentences are used as building blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation patterns from English to formal language (universal vs existential)
rubrics_metrics.description: English pattern 'everything in category has property' is translated as ∀ v (P → Q). English pattern 'there exists an object in category having property' is translated as ∃ v (P ∧ Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cautionary examples show the two patterns are easily confused: ∀ v (A v ∧ B v) means 'everything is an apple and bad' (much stronger), while ∃ v (A v → B v) is 'there is something which is bad, if it is an apple' (much weaker, vacuous if there exists non-apple). Several English→formal examples illustrate pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notational abbreviations and scope/precedence conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations: (α ∨ β) for ((¬ α) → β); (α ∧ β) for (¬(α → (¬ β))); (α ↔ β) for ((α → β) ∧ (β → α)); ∃ x α abbreviates (¬ ∀ x (¬ α)); u = t abbreviates = u t; negatives such as u ≠ t abbreviate (¬ = u t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parentheses conventions: outermost parentheses may be dropped; ¬, ∀, ∃ apply to as little as possible; ∧ and ∨ apply to as little as possible subject to that; repeated use of one connective groups to the right (α → β → γ is α → (β → γ)). Examples and expansions (unabbreviated forms) are given to show how to recover the explicit symbol sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polish notation for function symbols (convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Function symbols are placed at the left (Polish notation); e.g., '2 + 2' is written + SS0 SS0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This convention avoids parentheses for terms; spaces in examples are only for readability. It is part of the formal definition of terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique readability / unique decomposition (assertion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each term and each wff has a unique decomposition (unique readability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property is referred to repeatedly (used to justify recursion/definition extension) and will be proved in Section 2.3; it underlies the definability of term-evaluation extension s and recursive definitions on formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure / model (formal definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A structure A for a first-order language assigns: (1) to ∀ a nonempty set |A| (the universe/domain); (2) to each n-place predicate symbol P an n-ary relation P^A ⊆ |A|^n; (3) to each constant symbol c a member c^A ∈ |A|; (4) to each n-place function symbol f an n-ary operation f^A : |A|^n → |A|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: ∀ means 'for everything in |A|'; atomic formula P t1...tn is true in A under an assignment iff (s(t1),...,s(tn)) ∈ P^A. Universe is required to be nonempty; function symbols must be total (defined on all |A|^n). Examples (set-theory-language interpreted over naturals with ∈ as '<') illustrate how formal sentences map to English assertions about the structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction and truth in a structure (definition procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define |=_A φ[s] (A satisfies wff φ under variable assignment s: V → |A|) by: extend s uniquely to terms (s(t) for each term t) via s(x)=s(x) for variables, s(c)=c^A for constants, and s(f t1...tn)=f^A(s(t1),...,s(tn)); for atomic formulas, |=_A = t1 t2 [s] iff s(t1)=s(t2); and |=_A P t1...tn [s] iff (s(t1),...,s(tn)) ∈ P^A; extend satisfaction recursively for ¬, →, ∀ quantifiers. A sentence σ is true in A (A models σ) iff |=_A σ (no assignment needed because no free variables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes the notion of translating formulas into English determined by A and an assignment s. The atomic-then-recursive approach avoids informal English criteria and yields a precise mathematical definition of truth in a structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of effective enumerability via decidable relation on pairs (exercise remark)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set A of expressions is effectively enumerable iff there is a decidable set B of pairs (α,n) (an expression α and an integer n) such that A = dom(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an alternative characterization: enumerable sets are the domains of decidable relations. (Presented as exercise ∗9.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical caution about enumerations and nonmembership
rubrics_metrics.description: When monitoring an effective enumeration for membership (to semidecide membership), failure of ε to appear among the first many enumerated members gives no general way of concluding ε ∉ A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text warns that absence in large finite prefix (e.g., first 10^10 outputs) does not justify concluding non-membership; this is an anti-pattern regarding semidecision procedures and illustrates why semidecidability differs from decidability.
